knowledge:
- key_parameters: proband, mother, father=Sample IDs in the VCF file to define the trio structure ;; add_ratios=Logical flag to calculate sequencing depth ratios inside vs outside the event for quality control ;; BPPARAM=Parallelization settings passed to BiocParallel::bplapply() ;; n_mendelian_error=Minimum number of Mendelian errors supporting the UPD event to filter out genotyping errors ;; size=Minimum length in base pairs of the event to exclude short spurious segments ;; error_threshold=Maximum number of Mendelian errors allowed for a region to be considered in the recurrence analysis ;; min_support=Minimum number of distinct samples required for a cluster of overlapping events to be considered recurrent ;; max_dist=Maximum distance threshold used to cut the hierarchical clustering dendrogram ;; linkage=Linkage method used in agglomerative hierarchical clustering
- alternatives: None mentioned. The documentation focuses on using external BED files (such as SFARI.bed or Zenodo-hosted excluded regions) to mask or filter out recurrent/artifactual regions.
- when_to_use: When you have trio-based genetic data (VCF format with proband, mother, and father genotypes) and want to detect, classify, and locate uniparental disomy (UPD) events (maternal/paternal isodisomy or heterodisomy).
- pitfalls: Input VCF must contain only biallelic variants and fully called genotypes (no missing genotypes './.' for standard VCFs, and no sites where all members are homozygous reference '0/0'). Centromeres, telomeres, segmental duplications, and immune complex regions (HLA/KIR) can cause false-positive signals due to mapping ambiguity or high polymorphism and should be masked beforehand. Small regions detected by calculateEvents are often artifacts and must be filtered using collapseEvents. Highly recurrent regions across samples often reflect systematic technical artifacts or structural genomic complexity rather than true UPDs.

workflows.name: upd_detection_and_postprocessing
workflows.intent: Detect, filter, collapse, and annotate uniparental disomy (UPD) events from trio VCF files.
input: sample1.vcf.gz (multisample VCF containing genotypes for trio 1)
sample2.vcf.gz (multisample VCF containing genotypes for trio 2)
SFARI.bed (external BED file containing recurrent artifactual regions)
workflows.stages: 1. Load and preprocess VCF files using VariantAnnotation::readVcf and vcfCheck ;; 2. Detect UPD events using calculateEvents ;; 3. Collapse and filter events using collapseEvents ;; 4. Identify and annotate recurrent regions using identifyRecurrentRegions and markRecurrentRegions ;; 5. Visualize UPD events across the genome using karyoploteR
workflows.code:
library(UPDhmm)
library(dplyr)
library(VariantAnnotation)
library(regioneR)
library(karyoploteR)

#Example files
files <- c(
 system.file(package = "UPDhmm", "extdata", "sample1.vcf.gz"),
 system.file(package = "UPDhmm", "extdata", "sample2.vcf.gz")
)

# Define the trio structure
trio_list <- list(
 list(
 proband = "NA19675",
 mother = "NA19678",
 father = "NA19679"
 ),
 list(
 proband = "NA19685",
 mother = "NA19688",
 father = "NA19689"
 )
)

# Read and preprocess each VCF
vcf_list <- mapply(function(file, trio) {
 vcf <- readVcf(file)
 vcfCheck(vcf, proband = trio$proband, mother = trio$mother, father = trio$father)
}, files, trio_list, SIMPLIFY = FALSE)

events_list <- lapply(vcf_list, calculateEvents, add_ratios = TRUE)

collapsed_list <- lapply(events_list, collapseEvents)
collapsed_all <- do.call(rbind.data.frame, c(collapsed_list, make.row.names = FALSE))

recurrentRegions <- identifyRecurrentRegions(
 df = collapsed_all,
 ID_col = "ID",
 error_threshold = 100,
 min_support = 2,
 max_dist = 0.97
)

annotatedEvents <- markRecurrentRegions(
 df = collapsed_all,
 recurrent_regions = recurrentRegions
)

bed <- system.file(package = "UPDhmm", "extdata", "SFARI.bed")
bed_df <- read.table(
 bed, header = TRUE
)
bed_gr <- toGRanges(bed_df)
annotatedEvents <- markRecurrentRegions(
 df = collapsed_all,
 recurrent_regions = bed_gr
)

# Function to visualize UPD events across the genome
plotUPDKp <- function(updEvents) {
#--------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Detect coordinate columns
#--------------------------------------------------------------
if (all(c("start", "end") %in% colnames(updEvents))) {
 start_col <- "start"
 end_col <- "end"
} else if (all(c("min_start", "max_end") %in% colnames(updEvents))) {
 start_col <- "min_start"
 end_col <- "max_end"
} else {
 stop("Input must contain either (start, end) or (min_start, max_end) columns.")
}
#--------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Ensure chromosome naming format (e.g. "chr3")
#--------------------------------------------------------------
updEvents$seqnames <- ifelse(grepl("^chr", updEvents$chromosome), updEvents$seqnames, paste0("chr", updEvents$chromosome))
#--------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Helper function to safely create GRanges only if events exist
#--------------------------------------------------------------
to_gr_safe <- function(df, grp) {
 subset_df <- subset(df, group == grp)
 if (nrow(subset_df) > 0) {
 toGRanges(subset_df[, c("seqnames", start_col, end_col)])
 } else {
 NULL
 }
}
#--------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Separate UPD event types
#--------------------------------------------------------------
het_fat <- to_gr_safe(updEvents, "het_fat")
het_mat <- to_gr_safe(updEvents, "het_mat")
iso_fat <- to_gr_safe(updEvents, "iso_fat")
iso_mat <- to_gr_safe(updEvents, "iso_mat")
#--------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Create the genome ideogram
#--------------------------------------------------------------
kp <- plotKaryotype(genome = "hg19")
#--------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. Plot regions by inheritance type (if any exist)
#--------------------------------------------------------------
if (!is.null(het_fat)) kpPlotRegions(kp, het_fat, col = "#AAF593")
if (!is.null(het_mat)) kpPlotRegions(kp, het_mat, col = "#FFB6C1")
if (!is.null(iso_fat)) kpPlotRegions(kp, iso_fat, col = "#A6E5FC")
if (!is.null(iso_mat)) kpPlotRegions(kp, iso_mat, col = "#E9B864")
#--------------------------------------------------------------
# 7. Add legend
#--------------------------------------------------------------
legend("topright", legend = c("Het_Fat", "Het_Mat", "Iso_Fat", "Iso_Mat"), fill = c("#AAF593", "#FFB6C1", "#A6E5FC", "#E9B864"))
}

plotUPDKp(annotatedEvents)
